text:
maria_cs: Hey team — customer 'BrightLoop' is seeing consistent 429s around the top of every hour. They say it spikes exactly at :00 and lasts ~45s. They've escalated to account manager.
jordan_sre: pinging @alex_m and @priya_eng — can we triage? any recent quota changes for BrightLoop?
alex_m: I just checked billing/quotas: they are on standard plan, RPM/TPM unchanged. No quota bumps in the last 30d.
priya_eng: Do they send a large batch or cron job at :00? sounds like minute-boundary alignment.
maria_cs: CS confirmed they run a sync job every hour that fans out ~1200 requests in ~10s.
jordan_sre: that explains it. If 1200 requests hit a shared per-second window, gateway ratecap will trigger. Ask for request examples + request-ids from headers so we can trace.
maria_cs: Sent forensics: sample request-id X-Req-ID: brt-9f3a and a couple more. Also provided error response body: {"error":"rate_limited","code":429,"message":"request rate limit exceeded"}
eng_oncall_bot: (automated) linked logs for brt-9f3a -> forwarding to #eng-runtime for deeper trace.
alex_m: From edge logs I see the burst concentrated between 00:00:05 and 00:00:18. Routed to primary region, no fallback triggered. X-RateLimit headers show: X-RateLimit-Limit: 60 RPM, X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0, Retry-After: 2
priya_eng: Wait, X-RateLimit-Limit: 60 RPM seems low for their plan vs number of requests. But note RPM vs per-route or per-API-token semantics — the token is shared across many parallel devices.
jordan_sre: Quick repro suggestion for CS: run a spaced replay at 1 request per second for 2000s and see if errors disappear. If they still appear, it's a per-second or per-host limit.
maria_cs: Customer tried replay at 1r/s for 5m -> no 429s. So it's definitely the concentrated burst.
alex_m: Mitigation options:
- ask customer to jitter their cron (random 0-60s), or stagger shards
- apply temporary quota override on their token for top-of-hour bursts (if enterprise eligible)
- enable request folding on their client if possible
- update SDK to exponential backoff w/ randomized jitter

priya_eng: Also recommend server-side smoothing: we can enable short-term token burst buffer on their route for limited window. Requires ops approval.
opsbot: (automated) To request a temporary burst increase, open an internal ticket at https://redwood.internal/burst-requests with: customer_id, token, desired RPM, start/end times, reason.
maria_cs: Customer asked for exact repro steps so their infra team can validate changes. Want me to provide a curl reproducer they can run locally?
jordan_sre: Yes. Give them this (redact token):

```
for i in {1..1200}; do
  curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code} %{time_total}\n" \
    -H "Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>" \
    -H "X-Customer-ID: brightloop" \
    -X POST https://api.redwood.com/v1/chat/generate \
    -d '{"input":"ping"}' &
done; wait
```

This reproduces a tight fanout. For a spaced test, run with sleep 1 between iterations.
alex_m: Also ask them to capture response headers. If Retry-After present, respect it. If not, we can look at internal trace ids.
priya_eng: Long-term guidance: switch from synchronous fanout to a queue with rate-limited worker pool or use client-side leaky-bucket algorithm. Docs: https://docs.redwood.com/best-practices/rate-limits
maria_cs: Customer wants a short-term fix now. They're ok with jitter but want us to apply something server-side to avoid impacting current users.
jordan_sre: I can propose a one-off, timeboxed burst allowance: +2x RPM for 10 minutes rolling window for token brt-XXX. Need ops ticket per opsbot link.
opsbot: (automated) Created ticket RED-4287 for temporary burst allowance request. Assigned to @alex_m.
alex_m: I'll own the change. If approved, I'll apply a soft-cap increase and monitor latency/CPU on runtime nodes.
priya_eng: When we do this, enable tracing and add a canary flag so we can rollback if we see any degradation.
maria_cs: I'll coordinate with customer for exact window and confirm their cron time (they may shift to :00:30). Also shared the curl repro.
jordan_sre: TL;DR — root cause: synchronized hourly cron causing minute-scale fanout -> hitting rate limit. Remediations: jitter/stagger + short-term server-side burst or quota bump + longer term client redesign.
maria_cs: Thanks everyone. I'll update the customer and file a follow-up with outcome in this thread. :thumbsup:
